response.sql: SELECT AVG(avg_bytes_per_ms) AS avg_of_avg_bytes_per_ms, AVG(track_count) AS avg_of_track_counts FROM (SELECT MediaTypeId, AVG(Bytes * 1.0 / Milliseconds) AS avg_bytes_per_ms, COUNT(*) AS track_count FROM Track WHERE Bytes > 10323804 GROUP BY MediaTypeId) AS per_media_type;

assumptions.assumption: Tracks with Milliseconds = 0 are still counted in track_count. Their bytes-per-millisecond value is NULL (SQLite returns NULL for division by zero), so AVG skips them, but they still count as tracks.
Bytes > 10323804 excludes NULL Bytes, and Bytes * 1.0 avoids integer division. Milliseconds is NOT NULL in the schema, so no further null handling is needed.

alternatives.interpretation: Count only tracks that have a computable bytes-per-millisecond value (Milliseconds > 0), so track_count matches the tracks that feed the average.
alternatives.sql: SELECT AVG(avg_bytes_per_ms) AS avg_of_avg_bytes_per_ms, AVG(track_count) AS avg_of_track_counts FROM (SELECT MediaTypeId, AVG(Bytes * 1.0 / Milliseconds) AS avg_bytes_per_ms, COUNT(Bytes * 1.0 / Milliseconds) AS track_count FROM Track WHERE Bytes > 10323804 AND Milliseconds > 0 GROUP BY MediaTypeId) AS per_media_type;
